(ANSA) - ROME, 12 NOV - Extending 'ecobonus' tax credits to ten years in the 2027 budget bill is a 'South American-style' debt management tactic, the CEO of Italy's biggest bank Intesa Sanpaolo, Carlo Messina, said Thursday, drawing a sharp response from Premier Giorgia Meloni who called it instead a "matter of fairness". "Extending 'ecobonus' tax credits to ten years is a South American-style approach to managing debt owed to creditors," stated Messina during a hearing before the parliamentary commission of inquiry into the banking, financial, and insurance system. "What's included in the budget law—a ten-year timeframe—is simply unbelievable," he added. "I have a credit that matures next year, and now it's being pushed out to ten years, with no interest. "Under ECB rules—which we will inevitably have to address—this risks triggering issues regarding asset classification. How is it possible that this measure wasn't discussed beforehand to find alternative liquidity solutions?" Meloni responded: "I regret that these are being characterized as 'South American-style' measures; I don't believe they are.
